title: Codex versus LCA: small AWS SAM datetime API
hypothesis: At the same model and reasoning, both engines can build a correct small SAM API; the screen measures artifact correctness and elapsed time.
falsified_if: Either engine fails the frozen artifact contract or its invocation protocol; stop before scaling.
deterministic_outcomes: protocol status separate from artifact result
efficiency_outcomes: reported tokens and standard-equivalent estimated cost
decision_rule: Seed 90517; four runs total, randomized arm order inside each adjacent pair, simple control first. Maximum $4 standard-equivalent estimated cost between runs (one-run overshoot possible); 1080 active seconds total, 480 seconds per API cell. Stop after any failed artifact, protocol, or unknown usage. Both controls must pass before coding. A passing pair only justifies a fresh replication; no default promotion or general speed claim. The intervention is the entire engine bundle including system prompt/tools, not an isolated loop component. Codex CLI request configuration and JSONL are observable, but its wire requests and per-response usage are not; preserve that evidence limitation explicitly rather than asserting wire-level model activation. LCA records requests/responses. Original artifacts and all attempted usage remain outside task workspaces.
